Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (2)
They couldn't move. As if they were beasts facing a predator at a dead end, everyone except for a few Genesis Knights froze.
Kelliark was walking slowly across the sky as if on a stroll. With every step he took, people's hearts pounded.
Pssssst, shiiiiing…!

Just like the day he first appeared in the Empire's lands, the power of the ships, crushed by his force, was shutting down. Not only the lightning aura that moved the golden fleet but also the magic of the white fleet was seen fading away.

However, unlike that time, no one was clutching their throats as if suffocating. The reason was purely because all of the Coalition's Genesis Knights were present. The power of their existence had, to some small extent, checked Kelliark's influence.

He paid no attention to his subordinates who had stopped fighting and were kneeling on one knee to show their respects. The first things he looked at were the dead Genesis Knights of the Demon Army, the traces they had left on the battlefield.
In Kelliark's eyes, the final moments of their deaths were as clear as if he had been watching them with his own two eyes all along.

"I felt this last time as well, but this 677th dimension is quite a strange land. While nearly fifty Genesis Knights from our side have died, you have lost at most a few superhumans and some dust-like beings. Even with Van and Chiron Runcandel here, isn't this result excessive?"
The destroyed fleets, the dead Demon Army members, and the sealed Holy Army were countless.
Kelliark was marveling at that fact. At the fact that such a result could be produced merely through coincidence upon coincidence, obsession, madness, conviction, and pride.
'...Perhaps it's not just that. There might also be a kind of backlash, created by all those worlds rejecting me.'
As his thoughts reached that point, Kelliark let out a chuckle.
'So that's Kelliark Zipple... the leader of the Demon Army.'

Chiron was silently gauging the power of the Demon Army's leader, whom he had only heard about through words. He was curious about what kind of being this monster was, whom even Battle God Van had said
she couldn't defeat alone.
Endlessly vast.
As soon as he began to focus his mind and gaze upon him to grasp his nature, Chiron was able to reach the conclusion that measuring his power was meaningless.
It felt as if the universe itself was standing on the ground in the form of a human.
But strangely, he felt no sense of awe. It was as if he couldn't see that uniquely human, r
adiant something that comes from enduring pain over long years, overcoming adversity, and conquering death.
Despite being an opponent who could take his life with a single mistake, and who exuded tremendous pressure just by standing still, he felt no fear at all.
Nor did the desire to test his skills well up.

Chiron had spent his life yearning for an enemy who could push him to his limits. Before overcoming his demonization, some kings of the Black Sea could be considered plausible opponents, but in the human world, he had never encountered such a rival. Except for his ally, Van.
It wasn't because he thought he couldn't win. To Chiron, Kelliark seemed like a target from whom he could feel no joy in dueling or fighting.
"This must be how a farmer feels when facing a diseased and rotten land that can never be cultivated again, no matter what one does."
Chiron said, meeting Kelliark's eyes.

"Huhu. You mean I'm such an unpleasant opponent that you don't even feel like fighting? That's the greatest insult I've heard in my life. Yes, so you're the Chiron Runcandel of the 677th dimension..."
Conversely, Kelliark was receiving a fresh shock as he looked at Chiron.

The reason was, by far, that he was stronger than anyone Kelliark had ever seen. He had never personally witnessed the prime of Battle God Van in any dimension, so in his eyes, Chiron was clearly the strongest martial artist of all dimensions.
He was on a level that couldn't even be compared to any of the hundreds of Genesis Knights subservient to t
he Demon Army. Not even when compared to the Chirons of other dimensions, whose obedience he had always wanted to obtain.
"You are special, Chiron."
"You seem to be as well, in my view. You're completely different from the Kelliark Zipple I knew."

"With this dimension as the last, I have devoured all the Kelliark Zipples of all worlds. There were many friends who were lacking in terms of feeling a sense of kinship. It makes me think that you and I are a bit similar. We both became the most overwhelmingly strong beings among all the same people in those countless worlds."
"Kelliark Zipple, do you wish to earn my respect?"
At those words, Kelliark's eyes sharpened. The Genesis Knights and executives of the Demon Army who were watching the scene gritted their teeth at Chiron's irreverent attitude.
Recognizing this, Kelliark extended a hand into the air. Then, one of his most enraged subordinates was pulled forward as if drawn into his grasp and fixed in mid-air.
"Keoheok! Lo, Lord Kelliark."
Kidard Hall, who had reached the rank of Genesis Knight in the 173rd dimension, had followed the Demon Army's orders for a long time as the hegemon of that dimension.

"What has made you so angry, Kidard Hall? A man who, despite being a Genesis Knight, was so crushed by Chiron's energy that he couldn't even inflict any decent damage on the enemy... Now that I'm here, you're acting all triumphant like some ruffian who's called in his backer."
"I, I didn't mean that, keok, ghk."

"You are no different from a pebble rolling on the street. A Genesis Knight? Even if you combine all the numerous Genesis Knights of the Demon Army who came to strike the Coalition, they cannot match the value of one Chiron."
"I'm sorr—keoook, ghaaaaak...!"
Gush, crunch, grrk!
As Kelliark slowly clenched his fist, Kidard's body was seen crumpling like paper. His skin crumbled like rotten wood, his bones disintegrated, and his blood instantly dried up and vanished.
Soon, Kidard became a lump of pure white magic and fell onto Kelliark's palm, which he tossed into his mouth and swallowed as if it were a piece of candy.
"Still, it's not too bad to be used as a meal. How amusing."
"A disgusting sight."
"Surprising, Chiron. I thought you, of all people, would know that the essence of life is ultimately to eat and be eaten."

"It's natural for beasts to devour each other, and for humans to trample and kill each other. But you don't fall into that category, nor do you feel like a natural disaster. You are simply a being that should not exist in this world."
Beings to be protected, beings to be slain, and beings that should not have existed in the world in the first place. In Chiron's eyes, Kelliark was naturally the last.
It was a first. Even the kings of the Black Sea, if classified, belonged to the category of beings who deserved to be slain.
"Is that so."
Kelliark shrugged and looked down at Chiron.
"Then this time too, you have no intention of becoming my man?"
"Have the Chiron Runcandels of other worlds ever once submitted to you?"
"No. Regrettably."

"It is the same this time. Now that the one destiny of having to eliminate the kings of the Black Sea is over, a new destiny has simply arisen for me. I will cut you down, Kelliark Zipfel of the Demon Army."
Kelliark narrowed his brow as if genuinely bitter.

Of course, to him, Chiron Runcandel was not an absolutely necessary being. He already commanded numerous Genesis Knights, though they were significantly inferior in comparison, and he also commanded many gods.
However, this time too, Kelliark wanted to test his own abilities.

-Therefore, I want to test myself through you. To see if I, indeed, possess the power to change the unchangeable. Even if Orgal is still beyond me, at least the fate of a trivial being like you. If I don't have it, then I must not kill Malugia.
What Kelliark had said to Octavia after saving her.
The desire to twist the 'unchangeable in any dimension' was, in some ways, the greatest motivation that drove the Kelliark Zipple of the 33rd dimension.

"I understand very well... It is a painful thing, but on the other hand, a joyful one. That there are still elements in this world that can stimulate me. Once you are gone, there will be very few left, but it can't be helped. Now, die. The strongest knight in all the worlds."
Piiiiing…!
The moment Kelliark finished speaking, Chiron was engulfed by a ringing in his ears that felt like it was tearing his head apart, and he faced the sensation of his vision instantly going dark.
It was a fleeting moment.
But it was enough to die.
For the first time in a very long time, Chiron 'reflexively' raised his sword. He had focused solely on defense without predicting the moment of the enemy's attack, its trajectory, or its power.
Tzaaang-!

The blow just now had a power that would have snapped even Barisada in two in an instant if not for Chiron's aura. Chiron's vision vanished for a moment, and despite being completely unable to predict the direction, he accurately blocked Kelliark's attack with his blade.
"Kuhp...!"
However, his body was lifted into the air as he had to withstand the next blow, and his vision had still not returned.
"Father!"
"Chiron!"

Luna, Van, and Jin simultaneously threw themselves forward to cover him. But Kelliark's beam was faster than them, and Chiron once again raised his sword like a shield, relying purely on instinct. Tzaaang! Another deafening roar echoed, and this time Chiron was slammed into the ground, barely regaining his posture.

"Just like last time in the Empire, the father and son are both truly tremendous. I put quite a bit of sincerity into that attack this time as well, but to think it would be blocked like this. It makes me think I should have just come after finishing my recovery."
The smile was no longer on Kelliark's face as he spoke.
It wasn't because he had lost his composure after confirming Chiron's martial prowess. He was sincerely making the judgment to kill everyone here.
He was certain that he could.
